topSignals.title: FERC large-load show-cause filings due today across six ISOs/RTOs — the interconnection-rules reset that governs behind-the-meter SOFC economics is landing now.
topSignals.text: Per FERC's June 18, 2026 §206 show-cause orders (dockets EL26-67 through EL26-72), PJM, MISO, CAISO, ISO-NE and NYISO responses are due today, Nov 16, 2026 (SPP's follows Nov 20; protests/answers close ~Dec 16). Highlights relevant to SOFC siting and BTM value-stacking: PJM adds a 60-90 day interconnection study process on top of its already-accepted 50 MW large-load threshold; CAISO introduces a "Flexible Interim Load Interconnection" letting loads connect before network upgrades finish; ISO-NE's new track carries a $50k application fee, $150k study deposit, $10k/MW readiness deposit, and redispatches non-firm load above $250/MWh LMP — a concrete price signal for valuing on-site generation as a hedge. For Dominic: these fee/deposit/redispatch-price structures are usable inputs for the LCOE model's grid-alternative comparison. AIX Energy scorecard

topSignals.title: SoftBank takes a $3.7B writedown on gas-turbine equipment for an Ohio AI data center — coverage explicitly frames it as a tailwind for Bloom Energy's fuel cells over gas turbines.
topSignals.text: SoftBank posted a ¥768B (~$7B) half-year loss after a design-plan change at the site forced a "thorough reassessment" of already-ordered power equipment; GE Vernova (the presumed turbine supplier) fell ~4% on the news. Multiple outlets tied this directly to Bloom Energy, whose stock jumped 15.6% intraday on Nov 11 on a mix of this turbine-writedown framing, bullish CoreWeave demand commentary, and an unwind of post-election AI-slowdown fears. For Dominic: a competitor narrative shift — gas-turbine lead-time/design risk being cited publicly as a reason to prefer fuel cells — is itself a market signal worth tracking for INOCEL's competitive positioning, independent of any technical KPI. Bisnow · Motley Fool

topSignals.title: Project Jupiter (Oracle/Bloom Energy, New Mexico) hit with a second breach notice.
topSignals.text: Doña Ana County commissioners voted 4-0 on Nov 10 to issue a new notice of breach against the Project Jupiter developers (Oracle-led; Stack Infrastructure is on-site operator) for missing the Oct 31 deadline and filing an incomplete Q3 jobs report required under the project's $165B industrial revenue bond agreement — the second time in 2026 jobs data has been late. This is separate from the still-unresolved Oct 27 breach notice over the El Paso Electric backup-power connection. No sanctions specified yet; the air-quality permit hearing remains vacated since Nov 6 with no new date set. Albuquerque Journal

Status unchanged: elcoStack E3000 G2 platform (75% FC electrical efficiency / 90% with heat recovery, 33 kWh/kg H2 SOEC — vendor claims) in volume production at the 360 MW/yr ELCO I Tallinn factory.

Topsoe (priority): 81 days quiet on SOFC/SOEC specifically (since the Aug 27 H1 2026 results/SOEC pathway reset). Confirmed via direct fetch of topsoe.com/press-releases and /news — press feed stays active but entirely non-solid-oxide (newest: Nov 12 Sasol e-SAF Sweden selection).
Today's Tier 2 dedicated rotation (SolydEra, Mitsubishi Power), full Tier 2 sweep, and a Kyocera/Aisin check: no new item for any of the eight companies this week (Nov 9-16).

Today's Tier 3 rotation — cycle 10, round 2 (OxEon Energy, Nexceris, Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Miura, Weichai, Fraunhofer IKTS/Kerafol), plus two cross-company sweeps: no new item for any of the six, and nothing in the sweeps beat or neared (within ~5%) any row in SOFC_Benchmark_Records.md. One new SOFC/SOEC entrant surfaced during the sweep — see Benchmark-Neuzugänge below.
Competitor roster: SOFC systems for data centers

Bloom Energy: Deployed/signed at multiple named sites — Oracle/Project Jupiter, AEP/Google Cheyenne Fuel Cell LLC (702 MW/$4B, 20-yr PPA), Brookfield EaaS, Nebius (328 MW/$2.6B), Equinix (>100 MW/19 sites), Aligned "Project Phoenix" (2 GW), Hitachi (Japan), SK Eternix (28 MW, operational), NTT DATA (900 MW, global, shipments from 2027).

FuelCell Energy (incl. HyAxiom-branded products): Signed orders/PPAs — Fit Energy (up to 380 MW), Inuverse Korea (up to 100 MW), Texas CRA (75 MW), SDCL (up to 450 MW). Also hosting a DOE/national-lab-backed R&D testbed (StabilityMax) in Danbury, CT. No named commercial deployment live yet.
Doosan Fuel Cell/HyAxiom: Signed order — US AI data center supply contract (KRW 823.6B); supplies SOFC stacks to Reverion. No named data-center site of its own yet.
Convion: Pipeline-only/pre-commercial under HD Hyundai ownership; no named data-center customer.
SK ecoplant: Pipeline-only; no new named data-center deployment.
Ceres Power's SOFC licensees (Doosan, Delta Electronics, Weichai): Licensing/pipeline-only; no named data-center deployment via Ceres licensing directly.
Reverion: Pipeline-only — Doosan-supplied SOFC stacks for rSOC power plants (Germany); no named data-center customer yet.
Petra Power: Pre-commercial, no named customer; first infrastructure deployment targeted 2028.

EGEN Energy (China, new watch-list addition): Pre-commercial/early-stage; markets SOFC (distributed power, explicitly including data-center positioning) and SOEC (green hydrogen). No named data-center customer yet; small manufacturing footprint (100 MW/yr stack line + 300,000 cells/yr cell line) well below Bloom's or Elcogen's scale.
